industry: Performance chemicals and agrochemical intermediates manufacturing

frontMatter.introduction:
At Novopor Advanced Science Private Limited, we are committed to advancing innovation in performance chemicals, material science, and agrochemical intermediates. Our integrated approach emphasizes precision, sustainability, and scientific excellence across all domains—from advanced polymer technologies to high-performance chemistry.

This SOP Manual outlines the standardized operational protocols governing our manufacturing, R&D, and support functions. It reflects our dedication to quality, safety, environmental stewardship, and regulatory compliance. Designed for company-wide alignment, this manual ensures that every action taken within our facilities supports our vision of responsible and transformative chemistry.
frontMatter.objective:
This SOP Manual has been developed to:

Establish standardized and efficient procedures across all operational functions.
Maintain compliance with national and international chemical manufacturing regulations.
Optimize productivity while reducing risks related to health, safety, and the environment.
Cultivate a workplace culture driven by integrity, innovation, and continuous improvement.
Empower employees to execute tasks with confidence, purpose, and responsibility.
frontMatter.scope: This manual is applicable to all internal teams, external partners, and service providers involved in operations at Novopor Advanced Science Private Limited. It covers processes and procedures across: R&D, manufacturing, quality assurance and control, EHSS (Environment, Health, Safety & Sustainability), supply chain, packaging, maintenance, and warehousing.
frontMatter.reviewMechanism:
Novopor has implemented a dedicated annual review mechanism to keep this SOP aligned with evolving legal, ethical, and operational expectations.

Frequency
This SOP is reviewed once every 12 months, or immediately after any critical breach, regulatory update, or major infrastructure change.

sops.title: SOP for Effluent Treatment, Water Recycling, and Conservation

blocks.text: At Novopor Advanced Sciences Private Limited, responsible water management is a core pillar of our sustainability and environmental compliance strategy. As a specialty chemical and material science organization with significant water consumption across processes, we commit to reducing freshwater withdrawal, reclaiming and recycling treated water, and integrating eco-efficient water management technologies across our operations. This SOP provides the structured operational, technical, and monitoring framework for optimizing water use, deploying recycling technologies, and maintaining regulatory compliance.

To define the Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) for effective operation and maintenance of the Effluent Treatment Plant (ETP) and to guide water recycling, conservation, and optimization practices in alignment with Novopor’s sustainability objectives.

This SOP is applicable to all water management activities including collection, treatment, reuse, and recycling of wastewater at Novopor Advanced Sciences Private Limited’s ETP and associated infrastructure. It covers all manufacturing units and utility blocks generating High Total Dissolved Solids (HTDS) and Low Total Dissolved Solids (LTDS) wastewater streams.

blocks.text: The following detailed steps outline the standard operation of the Effluent Treatment Plant (ETP) at Novopor Advanced Sciences Pvt. Ltd., incorporating effective effluent management practices and integrated water conservation technologies within our operations.

substeps.text: Collect the HTDS effluent from various blocks or locations and transfer it to ETP storage tanks using calibrated flow meters. Record the Daily Flow Meter Reading in the format NAS-EH-018-F-07.
The acid effluent is acidic in nature and is collected from A-Block Part-2, C2 Block, E Block (M243 stage-1 and stage-3), and from M346 Acid and MMBC.
The base effluent is basic in nature and is collected from A-Block Part-1, C2 Block, E Block (M243 stage-2 and stage-5), and from Scrubber, M346 Base, and MMBC.
These effluents are distributed across designated tanks based on source type and volume. Treated water streams and segregated collection methods help optimize neutralization and filtration flow.

rows: A-Block (PPP-BP) Part-II Acid, SRS-1, C2-Block Acid, E-Block M243 Stage-1, Stage-3, M346 Acid, MMBC Acid.
C2-Block Base, E-Block-M243 Stage-2, Stage-5, Scrubber water and M346 Base.
A-Block (PPP-BP) Part-II Acid, SRS-1, C2-Block Acid, E-Block M243 Stage-1, Stage-3, M346 Acid, MMBC Acid.
Treated effluent water collected from MS Storage tank No:1, 2, 3 & 4(this is used as additional storage tank.
A-Block (PPP-BP) Part-1 Base, M243 Stage-4, MMBC Base.
A-Block (PPP-BP) Part-1 Base, M243 Stage-4, MMBC Base.
Treated water from SRS-2 through mixer-6.

substeps.text: Collect SRS-2 effluent and transfer it to Mixer-06 for neutralization.
Transfer the neutralized SRS-2 effluent to Filter Press-2.
Collect Filter Press-2 outlet water into a Nutch Filter.
Pump the SRS-2 treated water to Tank-07 or MS Tank-01 and 02.
Depending on requirement, pump the SRS-2 treated water from Tank-07 or MS Tank-01 and 02 to CETP or MEE.
Execute regular treatment procedures for HTDS effluent.
Take base effluent and neutralize it with acid effluent or HCL in the mixers.
Take acid effluent and neutralize it using CS Lye solution.
Collect PPP-BP (Part-1) base effluent in Tank-05. Similarly, collect M243 Stage-4 acid effluent in Tank-05 and send samples to QC to test Aniline content.
Pump the effluent from Tank-05 to Mixer-03 for neutralization.
Transfer the neutralized effluent from Mixer-03 to Filter Press 08 and 09.
Collect the filtered effluent into a 10KL HDPE Storage Tank.
Transfer the filtered effluent to MS Tanks 03 and 04.
If needed, pump the treated effluent from MS Tanks 01, 02, 03, and 04 to RCC Tank-04 for additional storage.
Pump the effluent from RCC Tank-04 to CETP or MEE.

steps.heading: Filter Press Operation and Handling of Spent Salt

substeps.text: Transfer the neutralized effluent through Filter Press into MS Treated Effluent Storage Tanks 01 to 04. Stop feeding neutralized effluent if inlet pressure exceeds 3.5 kg/cm². Apply 4 kg/cm² air pressure during drying.
Stop air supply to Filter Press and remove plates for unloading spent salt.
Remove moisture content from the spent salt.
Provide 20 minutes of rest for operators involved in salt removal after every 15 minutes of work.
Provide jaggery to all ETP staff at the end of each shift.
Ensure PPEs such as full body suits, organic cartridge face masks, gum shoes, and gloves are worn during salt unloading.
Dispose of the spent salt to authorized co-processors.
Record daily ETP operations in the log sheet – format NAS-EH-018-F-01.
Perform pump inspection using "Look, Listen & Feel" checklist – format NAS-EH-018-F-02.
Fill daily scrubber checklist – format NAS-EH-018-F-03.
Check scrubber blower efficiency monthly with anemometer – format NAS-EH-018-F-08.
Conduct quarterly fugitive emission monitoring via third-party.
Record effluent received from each block – format NAS-EH-018-F-04.
Collect LTDS effluents as follows:
Collect domestic sewage from septic tank sumps and QC/R&D wash water to VAT-01.
Transfer the sewage water into VAT-01.
Pass the sewage through Filter Press-10 and transfer the treated sewage to CETP.
Collect first rainwater into VAT-02. Treat through Filter Press-10 and send it to CETP.
Analyze LTDS for pH, COD, TDS, and NH3.
If parameters exceed PCB limits (pH: 6.5–8.5, COD < 8000 ppm, TDS < 12000 ppm, NH3 < 50 ppm), reclassify as HTDS and treat accordingly.
Record daily HTDS/LTDS disposal in format NAS-EH-018-F-05.
Record rainwater transferred to ETP in format NAS-EH-018-F-06.
Treated effluent from ETP is reused for non-contact purposes such as floor washing, cooling tower makeup, and gardening where applicable.
Closed-loop circulation systems are installed in cooling operations to minimize fresh water consumption.
Backwash water is filtered and reused where permissible under regulatory limits.
Rainwater collected in harvesting pits is treated and reused during non-monsoon periods.
Novopor utilizes a combination of air-cooled chillers and hybrid cooling towers to reduce dependence on water-intensive systems.
Cooling towers have been upgraded with water flow meters and cycle of concentration controls to ensure water efficiency.
Drift eliminators and automatic blowdown systems are in place to minimize losses.
High-efficiency valves, spray nozzles, and water-saving taps are installed in utility and process blocks.
Online monitoring of flow meters and usage dashboards ensure accountability across departments.
Procurement to verify every equipment order meets minimum 3-star water rating.

blocks.text: At Novopor Advanced Sciences Private Limited, protecting groundwater is a critical part of our environmental sustainability commitments. This SOP outlines all preventive and control measures in place to avoid groundwater contamination due to site operations, storage, or handling of effluents, oils, or chemicals. It ensures compliance with the APPCB and national water protection norms.
To establish standard operating procedures to monitor, prevent, and respond to potential groundwater contamination from site activities, with a focus on early detection and control.
This SOP applies to all Novopor locations where any chemicals, effluents, fuels, or hazardous materials are handled or stored. It includes areas such as:

Bulk chemical storage yards
Effluent treatment areas
Stormwater drains and groundwater monitoring wells
Utilities and loading/unloading zones

responsibilities: Oversee implementation of groundwater monitoring and reporting.
Conduct weekly inspections and maintain stormwater drains and dykes.
Maintain RCC flooring, dyke walls, and secondary containment.
Report any observed spillage or effluent pooling immediately.
Conduct monthly groundwater testing and analysis.

body.text:
No treated or untreated effluent is permitted to be discharged into the ground.
The treated water from ETP/MEE is discharged only through approved pipelines to CETP.
RCC flooring is provided in all areas where chemicals or solvents are stored or handled.
Dyke walls are constructed for all underground and above-ground storage tanks to contain any accidental leakage.
Rainwater harvesting structures are kept isolated from process discharge lines to prevent cross-contamination.

All stormwater drains are visually inspected weekly for any signs of contamination or discoloration.
Secondary containment systems are inspected weekly and after each rainfall event.
Rainwater collected is tested before usage or discharge, especially from catchment areas close to chemical handling zones.

Reuse of treated effluent water for gardening, flushing, or cleaning is strictly prohibited unless approved by APPCB.
No underground injection of waste streams is allowed.
Effluent holding tanks are checked daily for leakage or seepage.

Oil, diesel, or solvent spills are immediately covered using absorbent material and cleaned using approved procedure.
Drip trays are used under all temporary drums and unloading areas.
Damaged chemical bags or containers are isolated and disposed through authorized agencies.

blocks.text:
Groundwater samples are collected monthly and tested via NABL-accredited third-party lab.
Site groundwater balance is updated yearly to assess trends.
Third-party environmental audits on water use and discharge are conducted every 3 years.
In case of any non-conformance, a Root Cause Analysis (RCA) and CAPA report is submitted within 48 hours.
Corrective measures may include sealing of dykes, tank replacement, or process redesign.
Quarterly training is given to relevant staff on groundwater protection awareness and emergency actions.

This SOP shall be reviewed annually.
All monitoring and audit reports are retained for a minimum of 5 years.

sops.title: Emission Control and Environmental Nuisance Mitigation

blocks.text: At Novopor Advanced Sciences Private Limited, we are committed to mitigating our environmental footprint by systematically controlling emissions of pollutants and nuisances generated from manufacturing, processing, and ancillary activities. We recognize our responsibility in preserving local air quality, minimizing nuisance emissions (including noise and odour), and aligning our actions with best available techniques (BAT), sustainable development, and regulatory obligations. This SOP further supports our ESG (Environmental, Social, Governance) strategy and promotes transparency in emission controls.

To outline structured measures and technologies implemented to reduce the environmental impact of Novopor's operations, including controlling the emission of pollutants such as PM, VOCs, NOx, and SO2, minimizing nuisances like noise, odour, and light pollution, installing pollution abatement systems, and conducting third-party assessments to verify data accuracy and compliance.

This SOP applies to all manufacturing units, R&D laboratories, utilities, and warehousing facilities operated by Novopor in Andhra Pradesh and Telangana. It covers engineering teams, EHS staff, external contractors, third-party environmental auditors, and process leads responsible for emissions control.

responsibilities: Oversee all emissions control programs and audits.
Install, maintain and monitor abatement equipment.
Ensure process compliance and trigger action in case of abnormal emissions.

substeps.text: Modify production lines to reduce emissions at the source.
Use closed-loop material transfer systems to minimize VOC exposure.
Substitute high-emission raw materials with environmentally friendly alternatives.
Conduct energy audits to identify emission hotspots and propose design optimizations.
Deploy dust collection hoods and central extraction systems.
Install bag filters and cartridge-based filtration in drying, crushing, and material handling.
Periodic sweeping, road wetting, and vehicular movement restrictions in dusty areas.
Install ESPs (Electrostatic Precipitators) for PM10 and PM2.5 mitigation.

steps.heading: Control of VOCs, NOx, SOx, and Heavy Metals

substeps.text: Use of activated carbon filters and chemical scrubbers in reactor vent lines.
Install thermal oxidizers for VOC-rich off-gas treatment.
Maintain burner calibration and use low NOx burners for combustion zones.
Integrate automatic dampers and sensors for NOx control.
Ventilation zones fitted with gas detection systems for continuous leak monitoring.
Installation of sound insulation panels around compressors, blowers, and pumps
Use of acoustic enclosures, silencers, and anti-vibration mounts
Zoning and layout planning to separate high-noise and low-noise areas
Deployment of real-time noise monitoring systems with alert thresholds
Development of greenbelt buffers and vegetative barriers at plant boundaries
Mandatory use of earplugs and earmuffs in high-noise zones

Implementation of Noise Preventive Maintenance Program: Quarterly inspection of noise-prone machinery; Replacement of worn parts such as bearings, belts, and gaskets; Routine lubrication, tightening, and alignment checks; Post-maintenance noise audits using calibrated dB meters; Maintenance logs integrated into EHS system and reviewed quarterly
Compliance ensured with CPCB, ISO 14001, and Factories Act standards.
Implement localized ventilation and vapour collection systems.
Store raw materials and solvents in closed drums or vented tanks with activated carbon covers.
Deploy odour-neutralizing mist sprayers in high-risk zones.
Use negative pressure containment in odour-prone process rooms.

body.text: Novopor commissions certified third-party environmental agencies to perform annual on-site assessments across all manufacturing locations to verify:

VOC levels from reactors, solvent tanks, and process vents.
NOx and SOx levels from combustion sources and flue gas stacks.
Particulate emissions in areas with mechanical agitation or bulk powder handling.
Noise levels at sensitive boundary locations and within process areas.
Odour measurement via olfactometric or detection panel methods.
All instruments are calibrated before use and test protocols comply with CPCB, ISO 14001, and state PCB norms. Reports are submitted to Pollution Control Boards and retained in the EMS system.

blocks.text:
Reviewed annually by the EHS Committee.
SOP updates triggered post equipment installation or revised regulatory norms.
All emission reports retained for minimum 5 years under EMS documentation.
Review minutes documented with follow-up actions assigned to team leads.

sops.title: Sustainable Use and Management of Hazardous Substances and Materials

blocks.text: At Novopor Advanced Sciences Private Limited, we are committed to reducing the environmental impact of our operations by optimizing raw material consumption, substituting hazardous inputs, and implementing best practices for the safe handling, reuse, and disposal of hazardous substances. This SOP outlines our sustainability-driven approach to managing material flows, especially hazardous chemicals and related inputs, across all manufacturing and R&D operations.

To define a structured approach for minimizing hazardous material usage, adopting safer alternatives, and optimizing processes to reduce environmental risk, in alignment with global sustainability frameworks including EcoVadis and Indian regulatory norms.
This SOP applies to all operational units, laboratories, and warehouses handling hazardous materials or waste. It includes:

Process material optimization and recovery
Use of bio-based or alternative raw materials
Safe handling, labeling, and storage of hazardous materials
Substitution of hazardous chemicals with less toxic alternatives
Minimization and safe treatment of hazardous waste generation.

rows.definition: Materials derived from renewable biological sources (e.g., corn-based solvents)
Use of waste materials in industrial processes as fuel or raw material substitute

responsibilities: Oversee material substitution initiatives, monitor KPIs, and report improvements

blocks.text: The following procedures represent Novopor’s comprehensive strategy to manage hazardous materials in a sustainable manner. These initiatives support reduction, substitution, reuse, and safe disposal — aligning with internal goals and external standards.

steps.heading: Process Improvements for Reducing Raw Material Use

body.text: Novopor applies lean manufacturing and green chemistry principles to reduce the consumption of solvents, acids, and bases by:

Enhancing process yields and reaction efficiencies
Using high-purity reagents to minimize excess use
Automating dosing systems to control feedstock use
Adopting energy-efficient equipment that consumes fewer process materials.

steps.heading: Reuse of Recovered and Secondary Input Materials

body.text: The company recovers and reuses:

Packaging drums and containers (after decontamination)
Spent solvents via in-house distillation
Filtered salts and byproducts for use in secondary processes
Scrap materials from maintenance and fabrication operations
To track what materials are recovered and how they are reused:

steps.heading: Adoption of Bio-Based and Low-Impact Raw Materials

body.text: Novopor progressively substitutes fossil-derived or toxic raw materials with:

Plant-derived surfactants and biodegradable dispersants
Aqueous solutions in place of volatile organic compounds (VOCs)
Renewable solvents and green sealants in maintenance applications

steps.heading: Replacement of High-Hazard Inputs with Safer Alternatives

body.text: Our R&D and Process Engineering teams actively substitute:

Acids with buffered aqueous alternatives
Strong oxidizers with milder chemical equivalents
Fossil-based fuels with biomass-derived or hydrogen-based reducers

steps.heading: Minimization of Hazardous Waste Volume and Toxicity

body.text: To reduce toxicity at source, Novopor has:

Adopted closed-loop reaction setups to limit vapors
Used scrubbers and filters for fume extraction
Installed mixing systems to eliminate splashing and manual handling
Introduced neutralization tanks to treat residues before disposal

steps.heading: Protocols for Safe Handling, Identification, and Logistics

body.text: All hazardous substances are:

Labeled as per GHS and APPCB norms
Stored with MSDSs, secondary containment, and leak detection systems
Handled using PPE and mechanized transfer systems
Transported using approved vendors with emergency kits and TREM Cards

steps.heading: Treatment and Responsible Disposal of Hazardous Waste

body.text: Hazardous waste is:

Use of MEE, ATFD, and scrubbers for in-house treatment
Disposal through authorized TSDF or co-processing partners
Compliance with all documentation: Form-3 Register, Form-10 Manifest, etc.

steps.heading: Use of Less Hazardous Alternatives in Manufacturing

body.text:
Adoption of water-based chemicals in coating and blending
Use of alternative feedstocks such as biomass-based raw materials
Use of nano-filtration or enzyme-based catalysts for chemical efficiency

body.text:

sops.title: Information Security Incident Response & Breach Management

blocks.text: At Novopor Advanced Sciences Private Limited, safeguarding confidential and sensitive information—including employee records, R&D data, financial reports, and third-party information—is vital to our operations, reputation, and legal compliance. This SOP establishes a structured plan to detect, report, contain, and recover from any security incident or data breach, thereby protecting stakeholder interests and ensuring business continuity.
To define the systematic process for:

Detecting security incidents or data breaches,
Reporting and responding to such events in a timely manner,
Mitigating risks and preventing recurrence,
Ensuring compliance with regulatory obligations under Indian and international data protection laws.
This SOP applies to all departments, personnel (including contractors and vendors), locations, and systems that handle or store:

Store or process personal, confidential, or proprietary information.
Are part of internal IT infrastructure, cloud-based applications, or physical data storage systems

rows.definition: Any non-public data that may impact privacy, compliance, or business continuity

responsibilities: Leads response efforts, including system isolation, forensics, and coordination

body.text:
All employees must report suspicious activity (e.g., phishing, device loss, unauthorized access) within 1 hour.
Incidents may be flagged through security alerts, monitoring tools, or employee reports.

Affected systems are isolated by the IT team.
Access rights revoked, malware cleaned, and firewall rules updated.
Evidence logs collected and preserved.

Identify data categories impacted: personal identifiable info (PII), customer/vendor data, proprietary R&D.
Assess system scope, record volume, and potential damage

Internal communication via Department Heads and HR.
Legal notification to authorities (CERT-In, Data Protection Authority) if required.
External communication to clients or affected individuals must be reviewed by the Director – Information Security and Compliance Officer.

Restore systems from clean, verified backups.
Reset passwords, revalidate endpoint and server integrity.
Resume operations under heightened monitoring.

Conducted within 3 working days by the IT and Compliance team.
RCA includes cause, exploited vulnerabilities, mitigation steps, and corrective action plan.

Held within 7 days post-incident.
Involves reviewing response efficiency, incorporating lessons learned, and updating policies.

Phishing awareness

Reporter’s name
Systems affected
Data categories breached

sops.title: Emergency Incident Response & Product Recall Procedure

blocks.text: Novopor Advanced Sciences Private Limited prioritizes the health and safety of its stakeholders by ensuring readiness to manage emergencies, including contamination, illness outbreaks, or product quality failures. This SOP outlines our framework for preparing for, responding to, and recovering from such events, including recall protocols and customer communication.
To define a systematic procedure to:

Respond to emergencies affecting product safety or public health.
Execute product recalls effectively and traceably.
Ensure timely customer notification and regulatory compliance.
This SOP applies to:

All manufacturing units, QA/QC, logistics, and customer care teams.
All products under Novopor’s scope that may pose health/safety risks due to contamination, mislabeling, or regulatory non-compliance.

body.text:
Any employee identifying a potential contamination or safety threat must immediately report to the QA Head and EHS Manager.
Affected batch/line is quarantined.
QA initiates preliminary testing within 2 hours of reporting.

steps.heading: Recall Risk Classification and Response Timeline

body.text: To ensure effective, timely, and proportionate action, all product recalls shall be categorized based on the risk severity associated with the product health and safety hazard. The table below outlines Novopor’s standardized recall classification system:

rows: A situation where there is a reasonable probability that product use or exposure will cause serious adverse health consequences or death.

• Microbial contamination in chemical dispersants / • Mislabeling of hazardous ingredients / • Contamination by toxic impurities (e.g., heavy metals, solvents) / • Cross-contamination with incompatible substances
Notify within 12 hours / Initiate recall within 24 hours
Use or exposure may cause temporary or medically reversible adverse effects, or the likelihood of serious health consequences is remote.
• Incorrect batch labeling (non-critical) / • Shelf-life exceeded but no stability issue / • Minor packaging integrity loss
Notify within 24 hours / Initiate recall within 48 hours
Product use is unlikely to cause any adverse health consequences, but may affect regulatory compliance or customer satisfaction.
• Typographical error on label / • Cosmetic packaging defect / • Regulatory deviation not affecting product safety
Notify within 48 hours / Initiate recall within 72 hours

body.text:
Incident Response Team (IRT) is formed within 4 hours.
Roles are assigned and response is coordinated.
Draft official communication including:

Nature of issue
Product details (batch number, expiry, etc.)
Immediate customer instructions (e.g., stop use)
Notify impacted customers via email and phone within 24 hours.

Generate Product Recall Form (PRF) with traceability details.
Retrieve affected products via reverse logistics with documented chain-of-custody.
Recall tracking and customer response are updated in Recall Register.

steps.heading: Root Cause Analysis and Corrective Action

body.text:
Conduct RCA using 5 Whys or Fishbone diagram.
Implement CAPA (Corrective and Preventive Action).
Document in Incident Investigation Report (IIR).

File mandatory reports with applicable authorities (e.g., APPCB, FDA).
Submit RCA and CAPA documentation within 7 days of incident closure.

Final IRT review to confirm containment and resolution.
Lessons learned recorded.
SOP, training material, or process updated if required.

blocks.text:
Conduct at least 2 mock drills per year (1 for recall, 1 for contamination).
Train all employees annually on emergency communication and containment procedures.
Maintain updated emergency contact list for regulatory bodies and clients.

SOP to be reviewed annually or post-incident.
Improvement suggestions logged and tracked via Management Review Meetings.

rows.definition: Any concern or issue raised by an external party about the health/safety of a product.
The official digital platform where users can submit feedback or complaints.
Predefined process for routing and addressing critical feedback.
Action taken to eliminate the cause of a detected non-conformity.
Proactive measure to prevent potential non-conformities.

responsibilities: Receive, record, and route feedback to relevant departments.
Investigate product complaints related to safety and initiate testing or verification.
Determine regulatory reporting requirements and ensure safety logs are updated.
Educate customers on feedback submission channels and forward received complaints.
Analyze trends in feedback to identify systemic issues or areas for design improvement.

body.text: The following feedback channels are maintained:

substeps.text: Email Support – product safety concerns can be shared at productsafety@novopor.com, monitored daily.
Online Form – feedback form available 24/7 on novopor.com/feedback.
QR Code on Packaging – links users directly to the feedback portal.
Customer Care Line – Toll-free helpline 1800-123-NOVO (Mon–Sat, 9 AM–6 PM).
Distributor Reports – monthly feedback collected.
Sales Team Escalation – field teams use mobile tools to report client concerns to QA

body.text: All complaints/feedback related to product health and safety are

substeps.text: Logged into the Customer Complaint Register (CCR) within 24 hours
Automatically acknowledged with a unique reference ID
Categorized by severity (Low / Medium / High Risk) by Customer Service

body.text: For High Risk (e.g., illness, leakage, safety hazard):

substeps.text: Immediate notification to QA, EHS, and Regulatory Head
Product quarantine at client location may be recommended
Field investigation or product testing initiated within 48 hours
For Low/Medium Risk: Investigated within 5 working days
RCA (Root Cause Analysis) performed where applicable

body.text: Post-verification, QA/QC and EHS teams:

substeps.text: Implement CAPA (Corrective & Preventive Action)
Update SOPs or product use instructions if needed
Communicate resolution steps to the customer within 7–10 days.

body.text: Formal closure report shared with complainant

substeps.text: If regulatory reporting is triggered, Compliance files report with authorities (APPCB, FDA, etc.)
Records retained in the Safety Feedback Logbook for 5 years.
Bi-annual review of complaints to identify patterns
Improvements or re-designs proposed for frequently reported issues
Trends shared in Management Review Meetings

blocks.text:
SOP to be reviewed annually or after any significant product safety event.
Review team includes Product Stewardship, QA/QC, and EHS leads.
Feedback handling processes may be revised based on new regulatory norms, customer demands, or audit outcomes.
